problem: Sᵢ = ∮ ds/t is stated to be 'in mm, with t in mm'. ds/t is a length divided by a length, so Sᵢ is dimensionless. The worked example uses S₁ = 500 with no unit, which is right, so the stated unit contradicts the example.
fix: Sᵢ = ∮ᵢ ds/t over the walls of cell i, a dimensionless number when ds and t are both in mm (500 for cell 1 and 400 for cell 2 in the example).

problem: The procedure is self-contradictory and the closing sentence is wrong. You cannot apply the load through a trial point and at the same time force every cell to zero twist; zero twist rate is the assumption used to find the q₀ values for the (unknown) shear-centre load line. Also, the moment of the shear flows about a reference point does not vanish at the shear centre. That moment equals V·e, where e is the distance from the reference point to the shear-centre line, and e is what you solve for.
fix: Take the applied shear V through an arbitrary reference point, cut the cells and add q₀ᵢ, then choose the q₀ᵢ so that every cell has zero twist rate. Take moments of the resulting shear flows about the reference point; call the moment M. The load line of the shear flows, and hence the shear centre, lies at distance e = M/V from the reference point, on the side that makes the moments balance. Repeat for a second load direction if the shear centre position is needed in two coordinates.

problem: 'The point where the load must act for zero moment is the shear centre' repeats the muddled moment statement of Section 3; a student can read it as saying the shear-flow moment is zero at the shear centre.
fix: Say: the shear centre is the point through which a transverse load must pass so that the section does not twist; it is found at distance e = M/V from the reference point, where M is the moment of the zero-twist shear flows about that point.

where: Section 3, 'Walls that take no direct stress'
problem: 'Only booms are dropped from the shear integral' is confusing, because booms are lumped areas and never appear as a wall of length ds in ∮ds/t at all.
fix: In the idealized section the booms carry only direct (bending) stress and are left out of the shear-carrying path; every skin, web and spar wall carries shear, so all of their lengths and thicknesses stay in ∮ds/t.
